title: Tax Laws Amendment (New Tax System for Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015
short_title: Tax Laws Amendment (New Tax System for Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The Income Tax Rates Amendment (Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015 sets the trustee tax rate for unattributed income at the highest individual marginal rate plus the Medicare levy, ensuring that income not attributed to investors does not escape taxation.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The Medicare Levy Amendment (Attribution Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015 amends the Medicare Levy Act 1986 to impose the two per cent Medicare levy on trustees of attribution managed investment trusts when they do not attribute all income to members, ensuring that income does not escape taxation.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The bill imposes a 100% tax on trustees of attribution managed investment trusts that attribute excess tax offsets to members, clawing back the excess to neutralise the impact on tax revenue.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Labor referred the bill to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee for further scrutiny, citing concerns about potential loopholes and lack of transparency, while supporting its intent to reform managed investment trust taxation.

speeches.speaker: Bert Van Manen
speeches.brief: The Tax Laws Amendment (New Tax System for Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015 and related bills were supported to introduce a new tax system for managed investment trusts from 1 July 2016, with early opt-in from 1 July 2015, reducing compliance costs by $30 million per year at an estimated revenue cost of $125 million. The reforms aim to modernise trust tax rules, boost the funds management industry's international competitiveness, and attract foreign investment.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: The speaker argued in support of bills introducing a new tax system for managed investment trusts, modernising rules to reduce complexity and uncertainty. He stated compliance costs would fall by $30 million a year, the new system would apply from 1 July 2016 with a voluntary opt-in from 12 months earlier, and the changes would make Australia’s financial services sector more internationally competitive to capture opportunities in Asia.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: The bills create a new tax system for eligible managed investment trusts, reducing compliance costs by $30 million per year and taxing investors directly, modernising rules for Australia’s $2.6 trillion funds management industry.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: A motion was moved requesting the Senate to resume consideration of 14 specified bills from the previous session, with each request to be conveyed in a separate message. The bills covered water amendment, managed investment trusts, social services, crime commission, deaths registration, tax and superannuation, crowd-sourced funding, firearms trafficking, and parliamentary entitlements.
